findings: 2026-11-05: drafted for Mathematics 11 Unit 13 (owner request): English and a teacher-style Roman Urdu lesson; the book's content in order with our clearly labelled teaching notes; worked examples step by step with reasons; results verified with sympy.

Book correction: The book prints Newton's notation as f^{\bullet}(x) or y^{\bullet}, with the dot raised beside the letter like a power. In Newton's notation the dot is written directly above the letter: \dot{f}(x) or \dot{y} (read "f dot", "y dot"). Newton used it mainly for rates of change with respect to time, so in Physics \dot{s} is a velocity.
